public_rationale: A TechNave report dated 10 December 2025, citing The Information, said ChatGPT might have reached 900M weekly users. The Decoder, relaying The Information on 22 May 2026, said ChatGPT averaged 905M weekly users in Q1 2026, short of the 1B target. Magica reports that in May 2026 OpenAI again said more than 900M people use ChatGPT weekly, repeating its February figure. On these reports, usage stayed near 900M from December 2025 to May 2026. That fits 'growth has stalled'. On 27 February 2026, OpenAI reported 50M paying subscribers and 900M weekly users, about 5.6%. That small share fits the plain reading of 'struggle converting'. Two points cut the other way. OpenAI's published count rose from 800M in October 2025 to 900M in February 2026, but October is before the period set for this claim. OpenAI also wrote that January and February were on track to be its largest months for new subscribers. Under the contract, better conversion does not on its own contradict 'struggle', because the claim was not that conversion was getting worse.
limitations: The December 2025 figure is a hedged secondhand report of The Information ('might have recorded'), not an OpenAI disclosure.
OpenAI did not publish monthly weekly-user figures, so the month-by-month movement from December 2025 to May 2026 is unknown.
The user figures are rounded or come from unaudited reports.
The 920M February figure the speaker cites could not be checked against an available source.
The subscriber figure counts consumer subscribers only. A separate count of paying business users may overlap with it, so the exact paying share is uncertain.
'Struggle' has no stated benchmark. A 5.6% paying share could be read as normal for a free-to-paid product.
The result depends on reading 'stalled' as roughly flat from December 2025 to May 2026, not since October 2025.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI continues to struggle converting free ChatGPT users to paying customers, and overall user growth has stalled.
statement.document_title: News: OpenAI Had A Negative 122% Non-GAAP Operating Margin In Q1 2026, and ChatGPT Growth Has Stalled

from_speaker: "continues to struggle converting free ChatGPT users to paying customers"
context: "weekly active users hit 920m in February, the average for the quarter sat at 905m"
context: "OpenAI had expected to hit 1 billion weekly active users in 2025"
our_interpretation: He named no period. He describes an ongoing state as of 22 May 2026 and leans on Q1 2026 data compared with late 2025. I read the period as December 2025 through May 2026: the latest reported figures before the post and the late-2025 baseline he compares them with.

'User growth has stalled' (plain reading): ChatGPT's reported weekly active users were roughly flat over that window, with no clear rise beyond about 900-920 million and the 1 billion goal not reached.

'Struggle converting' (plain reading): only a small single-digit share of ChatGPT users pay. This is not a trend test. Better conversion than before does not by itself contradict 'struggle', because he did not claim conversion was getting worse.
Later growth (for example, 1 billion weekly users by mid-August 2026) falls outside the period and counts only as context.
criteria.support_condition: Reported weekly active users from late 2025 through spring 2026 stay around 900-920 million without a clear rise, and paying subscribers are a small single-digit share of weekly users.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reported weekly active users rose clearly (for example, by tens of millions) between December 2025 and May 2026, or paying users made up a large share of the user base.

evidence.excerpt: According to The Information, ChatGPT might have recorded 900 million weekly active users.
evidence.explanation: This report puts ChatGPT at about 900M weekly users in early December 2025. That is roughly the level OpenAI still cited in February and May 2026, which points to flat growth over the period.

evidence.excerpt: ChatGPT averaged 905 million weekly users, short of the one-billion target.
evidence.explanation: The Q1 2026 average of 905M is barely above the roughly 900M reported in December 2025, and the 1B goal was not reached.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI said in May that more than 900 million people use ChatGPT each week, repeating rather than updating its February benchmark.
evidence.explanation: OpenAI's own public figure did not move between February and May 2026. That fits a stall in the period before the post.

evidence.excerpt: ChatGPT has reached 900 million weekly active users, OpenAI announced Friday, putting the AI chatbot within striking distance of 1 billion. OpenAI also shared that it now has 50 million paying subscribers.
evidence.explanation: 50M paying subscribers against 900M weekly users is about 5.6%, so roughly 94% of weekly users do not pay. That fits the plain reading of 'struggle converting'.

evidence.excerpt: “Subscriber momentum accelerated meaningfully to start the year, with January and February on track to be the largest months for new subscribers in our history,”
evidence.explanation: OpenAI says subscriber additions hit records in early 2026. That cuts against 'struggle', though it does not change the small paying share.

evidence.excerpt: The earlier 800 million weekly-user figure reported in October means the published total rose by roughly 100 million in four months.
evidence.locator: section 'The public user count has grown, but remains rounded', paragraph 2
evidence.explanation: OpenAI's official figures show growth from October 2025 to February 2026. This is the main counterweight, although the December report suggests most of that growth came before December.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI’s suite of products, led by ChatGPT, has officially crossed 1 billion weekly active users.
evidence.explanation: Growth resumed slowly after the post, reaching more than 1B by mid-August 2026. This is outside the claim's period, so it is context only.
